title: TypeScript SDK: pragmatic patterns for AsyncIterable <-> Web Streams interoperability
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Ship a compact, well-documented set of conversion utilities and pattern recipes that make TypeScript SDK streaming ergonomic across Node/Deno/Browser by standardizing AsyncIterable-first APIs with optional Web Stream adapters. Deliverables: (1) stable helpers (toAsyncIterable, toWebReadableStream, pumpWithBackpressureProbe), (2) migration examples for existing customers, (3) test matrix and benchmarks for memory/throughput, (4) docs + snippet gallery. Emphasis: predictable cancellation propagation, retry semantics compatible with streaming, minimal bundle impact for browser consumers.

decision_log: Prefer AsyncIterable as canonical surface to simplify consumer ergonomics and interop with for-await-of usage.
Expose two small adapters: fromWebStream(stream, {signal?}) and toWebStream(asyncIterable, {highWaterMark?, sizeFunction?}) to cover both directions without locking runtime specifics.
Separate heavy polyfills (Node Readable -> WebReadable) into optional package to keep main SDK small for browser-first consumers.
Retries should be opt-in per-request; streaming retry helpers will provide hooks to checkpoint prefixes and rehydrate KV cache; we avoid automatic rewind of non-idempotent streams.
Backpressure probing will be conservative: default chunk batching target = 1024 bytes and max concurrent inflight = 2 for browser adapters; allow tuning via options.
We will provide explicit migration snippets that show: streaming->async iterable, streaming->webstream and a resumable retry recipe using prefix tokens.
